pool.text: The Auckland isthmus was settled by Māori, who valued its rich and fertile land.
Paramount chief Kiwi Tāmaki was killed in battle by Te Waha-akiaki.
Devastating intertribal warfare began, causing vulnerable iwi to seek safer refuge areas.
Paramount chief Apihai Te Kawau signed the Treaty of Waitangi.
William Hobson chose Auckland as the new capital of New Zealand.
The University of Auckland was founded and became the largest university.
A pipeline from Taranaki was completed to supply natural gas to Auckland.
Auckland was connected to the Maui gas field via a completed pipeline.
Government immigration policy began allowing immigrants from Asia into urban Auckland.
A five-week-long power crisis blacked out much of the Auckland CBD.
A Royal Commission on Auckland Governance was established to review local structures.
A forklift accident caused a blackout across northern and western suburbs.
Manukau City mayor Len Brown was elected mayor of the amalgamated Auckland Council.
Len Brown was re-elected for a second mayoral term at Auckland Council.
New electric trains constructed by Construcciones y Auxiliar de Ferrocarriles commenced service.
Two natural gas-fired power stations in Auckland were permanently shut down.
Auckland's port handled thirty-one percent of the country's container trade.
Phil Goff succeeded Len Brown as the successful mayoral candidate in Auckland.
Auckland Council released its Unitary Plan after completing a study.
REINZ reported the median house price in the Auckland Region.
